props: Sodium channel protein type 10 subunit alpha
Peripheral nerve sodium channel 3; Sodium channel protein type X subunit alpha; Voltage-gated sodium channel subunit alpha Nav1.8

Tetrodotoxin-resistant channel that mediates the voltage-dependent sodium ion permeability of excitable membranes. Assuming opened or closed conformations in response to the voltage difference across the membrane, the protein forms a sodium-selective channel through which sodium ions may pass in accordance with their electrochemical gradient.

references.title: Increased function of pronociceptive TRPV1 at the level of the joint in a rat model of osteoarthritis pain.
references.note: human OA synovium (TRPV1 raised) plus rat OA model: joint afferents sensitised, an intra-articular TRPV1 antagonist reverses the sensitisation and the pain behaviour

references.title: An update on targets for treating osteoarthritis pain: NGF and TRPV1.
references.note: review of the TRPV1 pathway as a target in OA pain; cited for the pathway in OA, not for trial efficacy

references.title: Cloning and functional expression of a human orthologue of rat vanilloid receptor-1.
references.note: human TRPV1 cloned, expressed in human dorsal root ganglia; capsaicin raises intracellular calcium in cells expressing it

references.title: The capsaicin receptor: a heat-activated ion channel in the pain pathway.
references.note: rat TRPV1 cloned by a calcium-influx screen in sensory neurons: a non-selective cation channel

references.title: Osteoarthritis-dependent changes in antinociceptive action of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 sodium channel blockers: An in vivo electrophysiological study in the rat.
references.note: rat monoiodoacetate OA: the NaV1.7 blocker ProTxII and the NaV1.8 blocker A-803467 reduce evoked dorsal horn firing, ProTxII only in the OA animals

references.title: Involvement of Nav 1.8 sodium ion channels in the transduction of mechanical pain in a rodent model of osteoarthritis.
references.note: rat monoiodoacetate knee OA: local NaV1.8 blockade lowers joint afferent firing during noxious joint rotation

references.title: Pain perception is altered by a nucleotide polymorphism in SCN9A.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.note: 578 people with radiographic OA: the SCN9A (NaV1.7) rs6746030 A allele goes with higher pain scores, and the allele changes NaV1.7 slow inactivation in HEK293 cells

references.title: Slow closed-state inactivation: a novel mechanism underlying ramp currents in cells expressing the hNE/PN1 sodium channel.

references.title: Human Na(v)1.8: enhanced persistent and ramp currents contribute to distinct firing properties of human DRG neurons.
references.note: human NaV1.8 in DRG neurons and native human DRG neurons: larger persistent and ramp Na+ currents, longer action potentials and higher firing

references.title: Action of MK-7264 (gefapixant) at human P2X3 and P2X2/3 receptors and in vivo efficacy in models of sensitisation.

references.note: human P2X3 cloned and expressed: an ATP-gated channel, agonist order 2MeSATP > ATP > alphabeta-meATP

references.title: X-ray structures define human P2X(3) receptor gating cycle and antagonist action.

references.title: P2X3 and P2X2/3 Receptors Play a Crucial Role in Articular Hyperalgesia Development Through Inflammatory Mechanisms in the Knee Joint Experimental Synovitis.
references.note: rat knee joint (experimental synovitis, not OA): blocking articular P2X3 and P2X2/3 lowers knee hyperalgesia, so the receptors work on knee afferents

references.title: Action of MK-7264 (gefapixant) at human P2X3 and P2X2/3 receptors and in vivo efficacy in models of sensitisation.

nodes.label: SCN9A
props: Sodium channel protein type 9 subunit alpha
Neuroendocrine sodium channel; Peripheral sodium channel 1; Sodium channel protein type IX subunit alpha; Voltage-gated sodium channel subunit alpha Nav1.7

Pore-forming subunit of Nav1.7, a voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channel that directly mediates the depolarizing phase of action potentials in excitable membranes. Navs, also called VGSCs (voltage-gated sodium channels) or VDSCs (voltage-dependent sodium channels), operate by switching between closed and open conformations depending on the voltage difference across the membrane.
Cell membrane, Cell projection, neuron projection, Cell projection, axon
